items.excerpt: Suno Studio 2.0 turns the browser-based AI DAW into something closer to a real production environment: native MIDI, automation, latency compensation, and a Studio Chat agent that can act on the project. It also lets users generate custom audio-effect plugins by prompt, inside the DAW.

MusicRadar's take on Suno Studio 2.0 focuses on Studio Chat, an agentic chatbot that can organise a project, edit MIDI and audio, transform sounds and spin up custom effects — the first time prompt-to-plugin has been baked directly into a DAW.

MBW frames Studio 2.0 as Suno's pro tier: MIDI support, an AI chat collaborator, and unlimited 32-bit/48kHz stem exports for Premier subscribers — while free and Pro tiers face hard monthly download caps starting September 3.

Suno is retiring all of its current AI models and replacing them with industry-built ones, adding tamper-resistant watermarking and fingerprinting via Audible Magic and Musixmatch Sentinel, and imposing lifetime/monthly download caps that gate commercial release.
BMG becomes the second major rightsholder to license repertoire to Suno, on an opt-in basis covering both training data and generated outputs. Universal and Sony are still litigating.

Beatport has expanded its Beatdapp partnership into a detection system that blocks fully or majority AI-generated tracks at ingestion, while still allowing — and tagging — human-led productions that used AI assistance.

Synthtopia's read on Beatport's AI ban centres on the line the store is drawing: 'a tool that assists human creation' versus 'a system that replaces it entirely' — and how blurry 'AI-assisted' still is in practice.

OA-Labs released Phosphor-1, a free macOS analog-style synth built for 'controllable instability', with a generative arpeggiator using per-step probability, groove and glitch. The developer — a designer, not a DSP engineer — built it in about two months with AI-assisted coding.

New AI chart-eligibility standards police the recording — vocals and masters, the things detection tools can measure — while leaving songwriting untested. The piece argues the industry has quietly redefined 'human' as 'human-performed', not 'human-written'.

MusicTech's weekly plugin roundup leads with Tamber V2.0 and its Tamby AI co-producer for spoken/written control of Ableton Live, alongside ReStem 2, Lucid, Monochord and Spectral — several leaning on ML for stem separation and synthesis without marketing themselves as AI.
